entityName: University of Augsburg - Organic Computing Group
entityDescription:
The Organic Computing Group at the University of Augsburg, Germany, has been founded in 2012, and continuing work which started at the Leibniz University Hannover in 2006.
This work investigates concepts and methods in the area of Organic Computing with a focus on self-organising networked systems. This includes software architectures for self-organising systems, distributed algorithms implementing self-x properties in such systems, for example building technical trust, sensor/actuator systems for interfacing ICT systems with their surroundings, and embedded machine learning and optimization in technical applications. Concrete application domains that serve as a basis for experimental evaluations include networked Smart Camera systems, communication networks, and vehicular traffic control. In the area of architectures, the basic observer/controller architecture and the multi-layer observer/controller architecture have been designed and evaluated extensively. The work on distributed algorithms for self-organising systems includes data management in mobile ad-hoc networks, e.g. consistency models and data distribution, as well as algorithms for sensor alignment/configuration at runtime. Embedded machine learning has been advanced, for example, when optimising applications at runtime based on context information using improved learning classifier systems or artificial neural networks.

entityDescription:
Stars Edge introduces the first Airbreathing Propulsion for Very Low Earth Orbits (150 - 250 km) enabling for a new generation of satellites capable of 3x Earth Observation Resolution and 5x the Telecommunications data transfer. The engine designed is the only in the market designed for Airbreathing and not retrofit from a previously existent and less efficient engines. Demonstrated in lab and using grant to push it to space testing within the next year/year and a half.
Engine doubles up as a clean and throttleable engine for existing satellites when retrofit with a propellant tank and system. The engine is capable of providing high power manoeuvers on demand and an economic manoeuverability mode with high efficiency and little fuel usage. The throttleable electrical engine is a first in the space market. To further set it apart from the competition other unique selling points of the product is its reduced emissions, cost and higher overall satellite security. This version of the propulsion system uses non-pollutant and readily available gas like Nitrogen.
The fuel used is 6% of the emissions and 5% of the cost as compared to current on the market alternatives like Hydrazine. It does not have a thermal signature or use pressure, magnetism or moving parts. Lower risk associated to the system allows overall less total satellite risk mitigation. The lower need for mitigation strategies (like redundant valves and sensors) allows the satellite to be lighter and reducing overall system costs. The power capacity of our product allows for the satellite to perform close proximity operations, collision avoidance and deorbiting manoeuvres.
The technology has been proved to be relevant for other global market applications of heat exchanging/thermal management specifically the synergy with the new electrical aircraft coming into service in 2035.
Stars Edge plans to tackle the space, the sky and everything in between.

entityDescription:
ABB Ltd. is a UK part of ABB Group and is headquartered in Warrington, Cheshire and employs 1750 people operating from 22 locations. ABB is a technology leader in electrification and automation, enabling a more sustainable and resource-efficient future. The company’s solutions connect engineering know-how and software to optimize how things are manufactured, moved, powered and operated. ABB was founded more than 140 years ago and has globally ~105 000 employees. ABB Ltd. has business lead of ABB Marine & Ports port operations and voyage optimization activities in UK.

January 2024 ABB signed the order with Portsmouth International Port to supply a shore connection solution for visiting ferries and cruise ships. The order is part of the UK port’s Sea Change project to design, build and operate a shore power system across its three busiest berths, the installation will serve two ferry berths – each with five connection points – and an additional berth shared by ferries and cruise ships. The system is due for installation in the fourth quarter of 2024 and expected to be operational by the second quarter of 2025. ABB’s shore connection allows vessels to turn off their engines while at berth, avoiding annual carbon dioxide emissions for the vessels calling at the Portsmouth International Port by an estimated 20,000 metric tons from 2027. This will significantly improve air quality in the harbor area while helping the port to realize its long-term environmental ambitions. To support this positive climate impact, ABB will continue to develop “Oversea – Fleet Support Center as a Service” as part of DECARDIS project to reduce emissions and congestion in busy waterways and ports further by optimization of voyage and port calls and reducing waiting times at ports.

entityDescription:
Unpredictability is usually perceived with a sense of uneasiness and discomfort. However, when it comes to secure our data, information, posts, pictures and whatever flows to (or from) the internet about us, protection relies on unpredictability. The impossibility for an eavesdropper or a hacker to break the walls protecting our digital life depends on secret keys, protocols and cyphering algorithms, namely the art & science of cryptography. Keys, essential to lock&unlock the doors, must be randomly generated. And true randomness implies unpredictability.
Random Power harnesses the quantum properties of semiconductors to generate a virtually endless stream of random bits feeding cyber-security systems. The principle is embodied in a platform of Silicon devices and benefits from micro-electronics advances; the source of randomness is endogenous and this is a genuine paradigm shift with respect to existing devices, providing simplification and robustness of the system; quantum properties of matter make unpredictability irreducibly unbreakable.

Random Power, supported by the European Commission through a grant within the ATTRACT cascade grant project (https://attract-eu.com/) and in collaboration with European Entities, embodied the patented random generation principle into three devices, including a high performance computer-on-a-board and an Application Specific Integrated Circuit (ASIC), a proprietary chip FIPS-140-3 compliant delivering the bit stream AES-256 encrypted.

entityDescription: IMENSUS UG aims to be the first geoscientific service provider for the emerging lunar industry. We are developing an autonomous rover for the seismic exploration of construction sites and resource deposits on the Moon. This rover will be used to generate high-resolution, near-surface geological models in our client's mission area. These models, combined with our comprehensive geotechnical consulting, will be offered to our clients. Our clients need these models to plan their more complex infrastructure and mining missions efficiently and with minimized risk. By doing this, we position our geoscientific services at the beginning of the ISRU (In-Situ Resource Utilization) value chain on the Moon.
